source.text: τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ὄρθρου βαθέως ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἦλθον φέρουσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα.

records.literal_gloss: On the but first of the week, at dawn deep, to the tomb they came bringing which they had prepared spices.

en.L: But on the first [day] of the week, at early dawn, they came to the tomb bringing the spices which they had prepared.
en.B: Very early on the first day of the week, at the first light of dawn, the women came to the tomb. They brought with them the spices they had made ready.
en.R: On Sunday morning, very early, the women went to the tomb. They took with them the sweet-smelling spices they had made.

es.L: Pero el primer [día] de la semana, muy de madrugada, vinieron al sepulcro trayendo los aromas que habían preparado.
es.B: El primer día de la semana, muy de madrugada, con las primeras luces, las mujeres fueron al sepulcro. Llevaban las especias aromáticas que habían preparado.
es.R: El domingo, muy temprano por la mañana, las mujeres fueron a la tumba. Llevaban las especias de buen olor que habían preparado.

fr.L: Mais le premier [jour] de la semaine, très tôt à l’aube, elles vinrent au tombeau, apportant les aromates qu’elles avaient préparés.
fr.B: Le premier jour de la semaine, de très bonne heure, aux premières lueurs de l’aube, les femmes se rendirent au tombeau. Elles apportaient les aromates qu’elles avaient préparés.
fr.R: Le dimanche, très tôt le matin, les femmes sont allées au tombeau. Elles ont emporté les épices parfumées qu’elles avaient préparées.

sw.L: Lakini siku ya kwanza ya juma, alfajiri na mapema sana, walikuja kaburini wakileta manukato waliyokuwa wameyaandaa.
sw.B: Siku ya kwanza ya juma, mapema sana alfajiri, kulipoanza kupambazuka, wale wanawake walikwenda kaburini. Walichukua manukato waliyokuwa wameyaandaa.
sw.R: Jumapili asubuhi na mapema sana, wale wanawake walikwenda kaburini. Walichukua manukato yenye harufu nzuri waliyokuwa wameyatengeneza.

vi.L: Nhưng vào ngày thứ nhất trong tuần, lúc tảng sáng, họ đến mộ, mang theo hương liệu mà họ đã chuẩn bị.
vi.B: Sáng sớm ngày thứ nhất trong tuần, lúc trời vừa tảng sáng, các bà đến mộ, mang theo hương liệu đã chuẩn bị sẵn.
vi.R: Sáng sớm Chủ Nhật, các bà đi đến mộ. Họ mang theo hương liệu thơm mà họ đã chuẩn bị.

ko.L: 그러나 주간의 첫 [날] 이른 새벽에, 그들은 준비한 향료를 가지고 무덤으로 갔다.
ko.B: 주간의 첫날 이른 새벽, 여자들은 준비한 향료를 가지고 무덤으로 갔다.
ko.R: 일요일 아침 아주 일찍, 여자들은 자기들이 만든 향료를 가지고 무덤으로 갔다.

pt.L: Mas no primeiro [dia] da semana, de madrugada bem cedo, foram ao sepulcro, levando as especiarias que tinham preparado.
pt.B: No primeiro dia da semana, muito cedo, aos primeiros raios da manhã, as mulheres foram ao sepulcro. Levaram as especiarias que tinham preparado.
pt.R: No domingo, bem cedo de manhã, as mulheres foram ao túmulo. Levaram as especiarias de cheiro agradável que tinham feito.

am.L: በሳምንቱ የመጀመሪያ [ቀን] ግን፣ ገና በጠዋት ማለዳ፣ ያዘጋጁትን ቅመም ይዘው ወደ መቃብሩ መጡ።
am.B: በሳምንቱ የመጀመሪያ ቀን ገና ጎሕ ሲቀድ ሴቶቹ ወደ መቃብሩ መጡ። ያዘጋጁትንም ቅመም ይዘው ነበር።
am.R: እሑድ ጠዋት በጣም በማለዳ ሴቶቹ ወደ መቃብሩ ሄዱ። ያዘጋጁትን መዓዛ ያለው ቅመም ይዘው ሄዱ።

decisions.choice: the first day of the week: the day after the Sabbath, our Sunday
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "the first of the Sabbaths"; the plural is used for the week, counted from one Sabbath to the next. The women had rested on the Sabbath, as the law required (23:56), and came as soon as it was over.

decisions.choice: at early dawn: in the first light of morning
decisions.reason: The words are "deep dawn", the earliest part of the morning, when the light is just beginning.

decisions.choice: the spices they had prepared: sweet-smelling oils and spices for the body
decisions.reason: The women had prepared them on Friday evening before the Sabbath began (23:56). They were put on a body in its wrappings as a last act of love and honor; there had been no time to do it when Jesus was buried (23:53-54).

decisions.choice: they: the women from Galilee of 23:55
decisions.reason: The verb continues the account from 23:55-56; the women are named in 24:10.

decisions.choice: the women
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since a new chapter begins here.

decisions.choice: On Sunday morning
alternatives: On the first day of the week
decisions.reason: Readable names the day in the way readers count the week today.

decisions.choice: sepulcro (L, B); tumba (R)
decisions.reason: The term chosen for the Gospels: "sepulcro" at Literal and Balanced, the everyday "tumba" at Readable, as in John 20. The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("il voit", 24:12)
decisions.reason: As in the rest of Luke, John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers meet stories, so Readable uses it throughout. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level, including the travellers' account in 24:19-24. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: manukato
decisions.reason: The spices and sweet-smelling oils for the body (meaning decision m3). "Viungo" today means spices for cooking, and "marashi" is perfume for a living person; "manukato" covers both the scent and the spices.

decisions.choice: "ngày thứ nhất trong tuần" (L, B); "Chủ Nhật" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 16:2: Literal and Balanced keep the Jewish count of days; Readable names the day as Vietnamese readers know it.

decisions.choice: "các bà" (B, R) for the women
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, as the English does; "các bà" is the respectful word for grown women, as the young man says in the Vietnamese Mark 16:6.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시- ("그분" at Literal); the angels and Jesus speak in 해라체, his followers speak to him in 합쇼체 with "저희", and Literal keeps Luke's one historic present ("본다", 24:12), through chapter 24
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (Korean style guide, sections 4 and 7); the speech levels are those of the Korean Mark 16 and John 20.

decisions.choice: "주간의 첫 [날]" (L); "주간의 첫날" (B); "일요일" (R)
decisions.reason: The forms of the Korean Mark 16:2 and John 20:1; Readable names the day, as the English Readable does.

source.text: εὗρον δὲ τὸν λίθον ἀποκεκυλισμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου, εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ σῶμα.

records.literal_gloss: They found then the stone having been rolled away from the tomb, \v 3 having entered however not they found the body.

en.L: And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb, \v 3 but having gone in, they did not find the body.
en.B: They found that the stone had been rolled back from the tomb. \v 3 But when they went inside, they found no body there.
en.R: When they got there, they saw that the large stone in front of the tomb had been rolled away. \v 3 They went inside, but the body was not there.

es.L: Y hallaron la piedra removida del sepulcro, \v 3 pero, al entrar, no hallaron el cuerpo.
es.B: Encontraron que la piedra del sepulcro había sido corrida a un lado. \v 3 Pero cuando entraron, no encontraron allí el cuerpo.
es.R: Cuando llegaron, vieron que la piedra grande que cerraba la entrada de la tumba estaba corrida a un lado. \v 3 Entraron, pero el cuerpo no estaba allí.

fr.L: Et elles trouvèrent la pierre roulée hors du tombeau, \v 3 mais, étant entrées, elles ne trouvèrent pas le corps.
fr.B: Elles trouvèrent la pierre roulée à l’écart du tombeau. \v 3 Mais, une fois entrées, elles n’y trouvèrent pas le corps.
fr.R: Quand elles sont arrivées, elles ont vu que la grosse pierre placée devant le tombeau avait été roulée sur le côté. \v 3 Elles sont entrées, mais le corps n’était pas là.

sw.L: Wakakuta jiwe limevingirishwa mbali na kaburi, \v 3 lakini walipoingia hawakuuona mwili.
sw.B: Walikuta jiwe limevingirishwa mbali na kaburi. \v 3 Lakini walipoingia ndani hawakuukuta mwili.
sw.R: Walipofika, waliona kwamba lile jiwe kubwa lililofunga mlango wa kaburi lilikuwa limevingirishwa mbali. \v 3 Waliingia ndani, lakini mwili haukuwamo.

vi.L: Họ thấy tảng đá đã được lăn khỏi mộ, \v 3 nhưng khi đi vào, họ không thấy thi thể.
vi.B: Họ thấy tảng đá đã được lăn ra khỏi mộ. \v 3 Nhưng khi vào trong, họ không thấy thi thể đâu cả.
vi.R: Khi đến nơi, họ thấy tảng đá lớn chắn trước mộ đã được lăn đi. \v 3 Họ đi vào trong, nhưng thi thể không còn ở đó.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 돌이 무덤에서 굴려져 있는 것을 발견했다. \v 3 그러나 안으로 들어가서는 시신을 찾지 못했다.
ko.B: 가서 보니 돌이 무덤 입구에서 굴려져 있었다. \v 3 그러나 안으로 들어가 보니 시신이 없었다.
ko.R: 여자들이 가 보니, 무덤 입구를 막고 있던 큰 돌이 옆으로 굴려져 있었다. \v 3 그들은 안으로 들어갔다. 그러나 시신은 거기 없었다.

pt.L: E encontraram a pedra rolada para longe do sepulcro, \v 3 mas, entrando, não encontraram o corpo.
pt.B: Viram que a pedra tinha sido rolada da entrada do sepulcro. \v 3 Mas, quando entraram, não encontraram corpo nenhum.
pt.R: Quando chegaram lá, viram que a pedra grande que fechava o túmulo tinha sido rolada para o lado. \v 3 Elas entraram, mas o corpo não estava lá.

am.L: ድንጋዩም ከመቃብሩ ተንከባሎ አገኙት፤ \v 3 ገብተው ግን ሥጋውን አላገኙም።
am.B: ድንጋዩ ከመቃብሩ ላይ ተንከባሎ አገኙት። \v 3 ወደ ውስጥ በገቡ ጊዜ ግን ሥጋውን በዚያ አላገኙም።
am.R: እዚያ በደረሱ ጊዜ በመቃብሩ መግቢያ ላይ የነበረው ትልቅ ድንጋይ ተንከባሎ እንደ ነበር አዩ። \v 3 ወደ ውስጥ ገቡ፤ አስከሬኑ ግን በዚያ አልነበረም።

decisions.choice: the stone: the large stone that closed the entrance of a tomb cut in rock
decisions.reason: Tombs of the time were cut into rock, and a heavy stone, often shaped like a disk, was rolled across the doorway (Mark 15:46). Luke does not say who rolled it away.

decisions.choice: the body: the reading of the SBLGNT, with no name added
alternatives: the body of the Lord Jesus, the reading of most manuscripts
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 and Codex Vaticanus among them, read "the body of the Lord Jesus". Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts have only "the body", and the SBLGNT follows them here. The title "the Lord Jesus" is common in Acts but is found nowhere else in Luke's Gospel, which is one reason some think it was added. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the large stone in front of the tomb
decisions.reason: Readable says what the stone was there for, since Luke has not mentioned it before.

decisions.choice: "발견했다" ... "찾지 못했다" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated Greek verb "found ... did not find" with one Korean root idea; Balanced and Readable say it naturally. No level adds Jesus' name to "the body" (meaning decision).

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἀπορεῖσθαι αὐτὰς περὶ τούτου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ἐπέστησαν αὐταῖς ἐν ἐσθῆτι ἀστραπτούσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the being perplexed them about this and behold men two stood by them in clothing flashing like lightning.

en.L: And it happened, while they were perplexed about this, that, look, two men stood by them in clothing flashing like lightning.
en.B: They were at a loss to know what this meant. Then two men were standing by them, their clothing flashing with light.
en.R: The women did not know what to think. Suddenly two men were standing beside them. Their clothes were as bright as lightning.

es.L: Y sucedió que, mientras ellas estaban perplejas por esto, mira, dos hombres se presentaron junto a ellas con ropa resplandeciente como el relámpago.
es.B: Ellas no sabían qué pensar de aquello. Entonces se presentaron junto a ellas dos hombres con ropas que brillaban como relámpagos.
es.R: Las mujeres no sabían qué pensar. De pronto, dos hombres aparecieron a su lado. Su ropa brillaba como un relámpago.

fr.L: Et il arriva, tandis qu’elles étaient perplexes à ce sujet, que voici, deux hommes se tinrent près d’elles, dans un vêtement qui étincelait comme l’éclair.
fr.B: Elles ne savaient qu’en penser. C’est alors que deux hommes se tinrent près d’elles, en vêtements éclatants de lumière.
fr.R: Les femmes ne savaient pas quoi penser. Tout à coup, deux hommes se sont trouvés à côté d’elles. Leurs vêtements brillaient comme l’éclair.

sw.L: Ikawa, walipokuwa wakitatanishwa na jambo hilo, tazama, wanaume wawili walisimama karibu nao wakiwa na mavazi yanayong'aa kama umeme wa radi.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakishangaa wasijue maana yake, wanaume wawili walisimama karibu nao, mavazi yao yakimetameta kwa mwanga.
sw.R: Wale wanawake hawakujua la kufikiri. Ghafla wanaume wawili walikuwa wamesimama kando yao. Nguo zao ziling'aa kama umeme wa radi.

vi.L: Và xảy ra là, trong khi họ đang bối rối về việc này, thì kìa, có hai người nam đứng bên họ, mặc áo sáng chói như chớp.
vi.B: Trong lúc các bà đang phân vân không hiểu việc này, bỗng có hai người đứng bên cạnh họ, áo quần sáng rực như chớp.
vi.R: Các bà không biết phải nghĩ sao. Bỗng nhiên có hai người đàn ông đứng bên cạnh họ. Quần áo của họ sáng chói như tia chớp.

ko.L: 그리고 [이런] 일이 있었다. 그들이 이 일 때문에 어쩔 줄 몰라 하고 있을 때에, 보라, 번개처럼 번쩍이는 옷을 입은 두 남자가 그들 곁에 섰다.
ko.B: 여자들이 이 일로 어쩔 줄 몰라 하고 있는데, 번쩍이는 옷을 입은 두 남자가 그들 곁에 서 있었다.
ko.R: 여자들은 어떻게 된 일인지 알 수 없었다. 그때 갑자기 두 남자가 그들 곁에 나타났다. 그들의 옷은 번개처럼 환하게 빛났다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, enquanto elas estavam perplexas com isso, eis que dois homens pararam junto delas com roupas que brilhavam como relâmpago.
pt.B: Elas estavam sem saber o que aquilo significava. Então dois homens estavam de pé ao lado delas, com roupas que lançavam clarões de luz.
pt.R: As mulheres não sabiam o que pensar. De repente, dois homens estavam de pé ao lado delas. As roupas deles brilhavam como relâmpago.

am.L: እንዲህም ሆነ፤ ስለዚህ ነገር ግራ ተጋብተው ሳሉ፣ እነሆ፣ እንደ መብረቅ የሚያንጸባርቅ ልብስ የለበሱ ሁለት ሰዎች በአጠገባቸው ቆሙ።
am.B: ይህ ምን ማለት እንደ ሆነ ግራ ገብቷቸው ነበር። በዚያን ጊዜ ልብሳቸው እንደ መብረቅ የሚያብረቀርቅ ሁለት ሰዎች በአጠገባቸው ቆመው ነበር።
am.R: ሴቶቹ ምን እንደሚያስቡ አላወቁም። ድንገት ሁለት ሰዎች በአጠገባቸው ቆሙ። ልብሳቸው እንደ መብረቅ ያበራ ነበር።

decisions.choice: perplexed: at a loss, unable to explain it
decisions.reason: The verb describes someone who can find no way through a problem. Fear comes in the next verse.

decisions.choice: two men: angels, who look like men
decisions.reason: Luke calls them men, as they appeared, but the two from Emmaus later call this "a vision of angels" (24:23). Two men in shining clothing also appear at the ascension (Acts 1:10), and Moses and Elijah stood with Jesus in glory (9:30-32).

decisions.choice: flashing like lightning: shining with a light that is not of this world
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for lightning (17:24). Jesus' clothing was "white and flashing" at the transfiguration (9:29).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to the sudden appearance. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: Suddenly
decisions.reason: Readable carries the force of "look" and the old storytelling formula with one word.

decisions.choice: mira (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term chosen for the Gospels: Literal keeps the narrator's "look" as "mira", Balanced and Readable let "Entonces" and "De pronto" carry it, as the English does. It is the narrator's word to the reader, not said to the women, so it is singular and has no plural_you span.

decisions.choice: tazama (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term chosen for the Gospels: Literal keeps the narrator's "look" as "tazama"; Balanced and Readable let the sentence carry the surprise ("Ghafla" in Readable), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "hai người nam" (L); "hai người" (B); "hai người đàn ông" (R)
decisions.reason: Luke calls them men here and angels later (24:23; meaning decision); Vietnamese tells it as Luke does. "kìa" (L) keeps the Greek "look", as elsewhere in the Vietnamese Luke.

decisions.choice: "그리고 [이런] 일이 있었다" (L) for "and it came to pass", here and in 24:15, 24:30 and 24:51
decisions.reason: Luke's Hebrew-style opening is kept at Literal as in the Korean Luke 3:21; Balanced and Readable leave it out.

decisions.choice: "두 남자" at every level
decisions.reason: Luke writes "men" and names them angels only in 24:23 (meaning decision); Korean keeps his word, as the Korean Mark 16:5 keeps "청년".

source.text: ἐμφόβων δὲ γενομένων αὐτῶν καὶ κλινουσῶν τὰ πρόσωπα εἰς τὴν γῆν εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτάς· Τί ζητεῖτε τὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Terrified then having become them and bowing the faces to the ground they said to them, Why seek you the living [one] among the dead?

en.L: And as they became terrified and bowed [their] faces to the ground, they said to them, "Why do you seek the living one among the dead?
en.B: The women were terrified and kept their faces bowed to the ground. But the men said to them, "Why are you looking among the dead for the one who is alive?
en.R: The women were very frightened and bowed down with their faces to the ground. The men said to them, "Why are you looking for someone who is alive in a place for dead people?

es.L: Y al quedar ellas aterradas e inclinar los rostros hacia la tierra, les dijeron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}} al que vive entre los muertos?
es.B: Las mujeres, aterradas, mantenían el rostro inclinado hacia el suelo. Pero los hombres les dijeron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}} entre los muertos al que está vivo?
es.R: Las mujeres tuvieron mucho miedo y se inclinaron con la cara hasta el suelo. Los hombres les dijeron: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}} a alguien que está vivo en el lugar de los muertos?

fr.L: Et comme elles étaient saisies de crainte et inclinaient le visage vers la terre, ils leur dirent : « Pourquoi cherchez-vous le vivant parmi les morts ?
fr.B: Les femmes, effrayées, gardaient le visage incliné vers le sol. Mais les hommes leur dirent : « Pourquoi cherchez-vous parmi les morts celui qui est vivant ?
fr.R: Les femmes ont eu très peur et se sont inclinées, le visage contre le sol. Les hommes leur ont dit : « Pourquoi cherchez-vous chez les morts quelqu’un qui est vivant ?

sw.L: Nao walipoingiwa na hofu na kuinamisha nyuso zao chini, wakawaambia, "Kwa nini mnamtafuta aliye hai kati ya wafu?
sw.B: Wale wanawake waliogopa sana, wakaendelea kuinamisha nyuso zao chini. Lakini wale wanaume wakawaambia, "Kwa nini mnamtafuta aliye hai miongoni mwa wafu?
sw.R: Wale wanawake waliogopa sana, wakainamisha nyuso zao mpaka chini. Wale wanaume wakawaambia, "Mbona mnamtafuta mtu aliye hai mahali pa watu waliokufa?

vi.L: Trong khi các bà kinh hãi và cúi mặt xuống đất, hai người ấy nói với họ: "Sao các bà tìm Đấng đang sống ở giữa những người chết?
vi.B: Các bà sợ hãi, cúi mặt sát đất. Nhưng hai người ấy nói với họ: "Sao các bà tìm Đấng đang sống ở giữa những người chết?
vi.R: Các bà rất sợ hãi và cúi mặt sát đất. Hai người ấy nói với họ: "Sao các bà lại đến nơi của người chết mà tìm Đấng đang sống?

ko.L: 그들이 두려워하여 얼굴을 땅으로 숙이자, 그 사람들이 그들에게 말했다. "너희는 어찌하여 살아 계신 분을 죽은 사람들 가운데서 찾느냐?
ko.B: 여자들은 무서워서 얼굴을 땅에 숙였다. 그러자 그 남자들이 여자들에게 말했다. "어찌하여 너희는 살아 계신 분을 죽은 사람들 가운데서 찾고 있느냐?
ko.R: 여자들은 너무 무서워서 땅에 엎드려 얼굴을 숙였다. 그 남자들이 여자들에게 말했다. "너희는 왜 살아 계신 분을 죽은 사람들이 있는 곳에서 찾고 있느냐?

pt.L: E, ficando elas cheias de medo e inclinando o rosto para o chão, eles lhes disseram: "Por que vocês procuram o que vive entre os mortos?
pt.B: As mulheres ficaram aterrorizadas e mantinham o rosto inclinado para o chão. Mas os homens lhes disseram: "Por que vocês procuram entre os mortos aquele que está vivo?
pt.R: As mulheres ficaram com muito medo e se curvaram com o rosto no chão. Os homens disseram a elas: "Por que vocês estão procurando alguém que está vivo num lugar de gente morta?

am.L: እነርሱም ፈርተው ፊታቸውን ወደ ምድር ዝቅ ባደረጉ ጊዜ እንዲህ አሉአቸው፦ «ሕያው የሆነውን ከሙታን ጋር ለምን ትፈልጋላችሁ?
am.B: ሴቶቹ እጅግ ፈሩ፤ ፊታቸውንም ወደ ምድር ዝቅ አደረጉ። ሰዎቹ ግን እንዲህ አሉአቸው፦ «ሕያው የሆነውን በሙታን መካከል ለምን ትፈልጋላችሁ?
am.R: ሴቶቹ በጣም ፈሩ፤ ፊታቸውንም ወደ መሬት አቀርቅረው ጎንበስ አሉ። ሰዎቹም እንዲህ አሉአቸው፦ «በሕይወት ያለውን ሰው የሞቱ ሰዎች ባሉበት ቦታ ለምን ትፈልጋላችሁ?

decisions.choice: bowing their faces to the ground: a sign of fear and respect before a heavenly being
decisions.reason: People bow low when they meet a messenger from God (Daniel 8:17). The women cannot look at the men.

decisions.choice: the living one: one person who is alive, Jesus
alternatives: the living, meaning living people in general
decisions.reason: The word is singular and masculine, "the one who lives". The question is about Jesus, who is alive; the tomb is a place for the dead.

decisions.choice: Why do you seek the living one among the dead: a gentle rebuke
decisions.reason: The question says that the women are looking in the wrong place. In Acts Jesus is "the Author of life" (Acts 3:15), and "the living one" echoes how Scripture speaks of the living God.

decisions.choice: the men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who spoke, since the women are the subject of the first half of the sentence.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the plural_you setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. Every plural "you" in the chapter takes the setting.

decisions.choice: "Đấng đang sống" for "the living one"; "các bà" for the women
decisions.reason: The living one is Jesus (meaning decision), and the heavenly messengers speak of him with the reverent "Đấng"; they address the women as the young man does in the Vietnamese Mark 16:6.

decisions.choice: The two men speak to the women in 해라체 and honour Jesus ("살아 계신 분", "계시지 않는다", "살아나셨다")
decisions.reason: As the young man in the Korean Mark 16:6: messengers from God speak with authority and with honour for the risen one.

source.text: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἀλλὰ ἠγέρθη.

records.literal_gloss: Not he is here, but he has been raised.

en.L: He is not here, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been raised.
en.B: He is not here; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been raised.
en.R: He is not here. He has been raised to life!

es.L: No está aquí, sino que ha sido resucitado.
es.B: No está aquí; ha sido resucitado.
es.R: No está aquí. ¡Ha sido devuelto a la vida!

fr.L: Il n’est pas ici, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été ressuscité.
fr.B: Il n’est pas ici ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a été ressuscité.
fr.R: Il n’est pas ici. Il a été ramené à la vie !

sw.L: Hayupo hapa, bali amefufuliwa.
sw.B: Hayupo hapa; amefufuliwa.
sw.R: Hayupo hapa. Amefufuliwa, yu hai!

vi.L: Ngài không ở đây, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã được làm cho sống lại.
vi.B: Ngài không ở đây; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã được làm cho sống lại.
vi.R: Ngài không có ở đây. Đức Chúa Trời đã khiến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sống lại!

ko.L: 그분은 여기에 계시지 않고, 살아나셨다.
ko.B: 그분은 여기 계시지 않는다. 살아나셨다.
ko.R: 그분은 여기 계시지 않는다. 하나님께서 그분을 다시 살리셨다!

pt.L: Ele não está aqui, mas foi ressuscitado.
pt.B: Ele não está aqui; foi ressuscitado.
pt.R: Ele não está aqui. Ele foi ressuscitado e está vivo!

am.L: እዚህ የለም፤ ነገር ግን ተነሥቷል።
am.B: እዚህ የለም፤ ተነሥቷል።
am.R: እዚህ የለም። እግዚአብሔር ከሞት አስነሥቶታል!

decisions.choice: the sentence is included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the sentence is left out, as in Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 among them, have these words. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts lack them. Some think they were added from Mark 16:6 or Matthew 28:6, but the wording here is not quite the same as either. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he has been raised: God has raised him
alternatives: he has risen by his own power
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, the form Luke uses for God's act of raising Jesus (9:22; 24:34; Acts 3:15). Jesus also speaks of himself as rising (18:33; 24:7, 46); both are true.

decisions.choice: raised to life
decisions.reason: Readable says what "raised" means here.

decisions.choice: ha sido resucitado, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English "he" takes the setting. Spanish leaves the subject in the verb and joins some object pronouns to it, so the setting covers only separate pronouns and possessives (él, lo, le, su, tú, mí). Spanish therefore has fewer spans than English through the chapter. The passive keeps God as the one who raised him (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on amefufuliwa (he has been raised)
decisions.reason: The English "he" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the verb prefix, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives (yeye, mwenyewe, wake, yangu, mimi, naye). Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English through the chapter. The passive keeps God as the one who raised him (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "đã được làm cho sống lại" (L, B); "Đức Chúa Trời đã khiến ... sống lại" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 16:6: the passive is God's act (meaning decision); Readable names God.

decisions.choice: "살아나셨다" (L, B); "하나님께서 그분을 다시 살리셨다" (R)
decisions.reason: The passive means that God raised him (meaning decision); Korean has no natural passive of "raise", so Literal and Balanced use the usual verb, and Readable names God, as in the Korean Mark 16:6.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic
alternatives: Marking pronouns for God and Jesus in some other way
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for Jesus in the English of this chapter, first here, has nothing to change in Amharic; "he" is carried by the verb (ተነሥቷል).

decisions.choice: "ተነሥቷል" (he has risen, been raised) (L, B); "እግዚአብሔር ከሞት አስነሥቶታል" (God has raised him from death) (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek passive means that God raised him; Amharic "ተነሥቷል" can be read either way, so Readable names God as the one who raised him, as in Matthew 28:6.

source.text: μνήσθητε ὡς ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ, λέγων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅτι δεῖ παραδοθῆναι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ σταυρωθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: Remember how he spoke to you yet being in the Galilee, \v 7 saying the Son of Man that it is necessary to be delivered into hands of men sinful and to be crucified and the third day to rise.

en.L: Remember how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to you while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still in Galilee, \v 7 saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into [the] hands of sinful {{gender:people|men}} and be crucified and on the third day rise."
en.B: Remember what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still in Galilee. \v 7 He said that the Son of Man had to be handed over to sinful {{gender:people|men}} and be crucified, and on the third day rise again."
en.R: Remember what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you back in Galilee. \v 7 He said, 'The Son of Man must be handed over to sinful {{gender:people|men}}. They will nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross. But on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise from death.'"

es.L: {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} cómo {{plural_you:les|os}} habló cuando todavía estaba en Galilea, \v 7 diciendo que el Hijo del Hombre debe ser entregado en manos de {{gender:personas pecadoras|hombres pecadores}} y ser crucificado y al tercer día resucitar».
es.B: {{plural_you:Recuerden|Recordad}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo cuando aún estaba en Galilea: \v 7 que el Hijo del Hombre tenía que ser entregado a {{gender:personas pecadoras|hombres pecadores}} y ser crucificado, y que al tercer día resucitaría».
es.R: {{plural_you:Acuérdense|Acordaos}} de lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} dijo allá en Galilea. \v 7 Dijo: “El Hijo del Hombre tiene que ser entregado a {{gender:gente pecadora|hombres pecadores}}. Ellos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} clavarán en una cruz. Pero al tercer día resucitará de la muerte”».

fr.L: Souvenez-vous comment {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a parlé quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était encore en Galilée, \v 7 en disant que le Fils de l’homme doit être livré entre les mains d’{{gender:humains|hommes}} pécheurs, et être crucifié, et, le troisième jour, ressusciter. »
fr.B: Rappelez-vous ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a dit quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était encore en Galilée. \v 7 Il a dit que le Fils de l’homme devait être livré à des {{gender:humains|hommes}} pécheurs et être crucifié, et que le troisième jour {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ressusciterait. »
fr.R: Rappelez-vous ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a dit quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était là-bas, en Galilée. \v 7 Il a dit : “Le Fils de l’homme doit être livré à des {{gender:humains|hommes}} pécheurs. Ils vont {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} clouer sur une croix. Mais le troisième jour, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} va revenir à la vie.” »

sw.L: Kumbukeni jinsi alivyowaambia alipokuwa bado yuko Galilaya, \v 7 akisema kwamba Mwana wa Adamu lazima atiwe mikononi mwa watu wenye dhambi, na kusulubiwa, na siku ya tatu kufufuka."
sw.B: Kumbukeni alivyowaambia alipokuwa bado yuko Galilaya: \v 7 kwamba ilimpasa Mwana wa Adamu akabidhiwe mikononi mwa watu wenye dhambi, asulubiwe, kisha siku ya tatu afufuke."
sw.R: Kumbukeni alichowaambia kule Galilaya. \v 7 Alisema, 'Mwana wa Adamu lazima akabidhiwe kwa watu wenye dhambi. Watamgongomea msalabani. Lakini siku ya tatu atafufuka kutoka kwa wafu.'"

vi.L: Hãy nhớ lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với các bà thế nào khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} còn ở Ga-li-lê, \v 7 rằng Con Người phải bị nộp vào tay những người tội lỗi, bị đóng đinh, và ngày thứ ba sống lại."
vi.B: Hãy nhớ lại điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với các bà khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} còn ở Ga-li-lê. \v 7 Ngài đã nói rằng Con Người phải bị nộp vào tay những người tội lỗi, phải bị đóng đinh, và đến ngày thứ ba thì sống lại."
vi.R: Hãy nhớ lại điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói với các bà khi còn ở Ga-li-lê. \v 7 Ngài đã nói: 'Con Người phải bị nộp vào tay những kẻ tội lỗi. Họ sẽ đóng đinh Con Người trên cây thập tự. Nhưng đến ngày thứ ba, Con Người sẽ sống lại từ cõi chết.'"

ko.L: 그분이 아직 갈릴리에 계실 때에 너희에게 어떻게 말씀하셨는지 기억하여라. \v 7 인자가 반드시 죄인인 사람들의 손에 넘겨져 십자가에 못 박히고, 사흘째 되는 날에 살아나야 한다고 하셨다."
ko.B: 그분이 아직 갈릴리에 계실 때에 너희에게 하신 말씀을 기억하여라. \v 7 인자가 죄인들의 손에 넘겨져 십자가에 못 박히고, 사흘째 되는 날에 다시 살아나야 한다고 하셨다."
ko.R: 그분이 갈릴리에 계실 때 너희에게 하신 말씀을 기억하여라. \v 7 그분은 이렇게 말씀하셨다. '인자는 죄인들의 손에 넘겨질 것이다. 그들이 인자를 십자가에 못 박을 것이다. 그러나 인자는 사흘째 되는 날에 다시 살아날 것이다.'"

pt.L: Lembrem-se de como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes falou quando ainda estava na Galileia, \v 7 dizendo que era necessário que o Filho do Homem fosse entregue nas mãos de {{gender:pessoas pecadoras|homens pecadores}}, e fosse crucificado, e ao terceiro dia ressuscitasse."
pt.B: Lembrem-se do que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse quando ainda estava na Galileia. \v 7 Ele disse que o Filho do Homem tinha de ser entregue nas mãos de {{gender:pessoas pecadoras|homens pecadores}} e ser crucificado, e que ao terceiro dia ressuscitaria."
pt.R: Lembrem-se do que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse a vocês lá na Galileia. \v 7 Ele disse: 'O Filho do Homem precisa ser entregue a {{gender:pessoas pecadoras|homens pecadores}}. Vão pregá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} numa cruz. Mas no terceiro dia {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai ressuscitar.'"

am.L: ገና በገሊላ ሳለ እንዴት እንደ ተናገራችሁ አስታውሱ፤ \v 7 የሰው ልጅ በኃጢአተኞች ሰዎች እጅ ተላልፎ ሊሰጥ፣ ሊሰቀልም፣ በሦስተኛውም ቀን ሊነሣ ይገባዋል ብሎ ነበር።»
am.B: ገና በገሊላ ሳለ የነገራችሁን አስታውሱ። \v 7 የሰው ልጅ ለኃጢአተኞች ሰዎች ተላልፎ ሊሰጥና ሊሰቀል፣ በሦስተኛውም ቀን ሊነሣ እንደሚገባው ነግሯችሁ ነበር።»
am.R: በገሊላ ሳለ የነገራችሁን አስታውሱ። \v 7 እንዲህ ብሎ ነበር፦ “የሰው ልጅ ለኃጢአተኞች ሰዎች ተላልፎ ሊሰጥ ይገባዋል። እነርሱም በመስቀል ላይ ይቸነክሩታል። በሦስተኛው ቀን ግን ከሞት ይነሣል።”»

decisions.choice: how he spoke to you in Galilee: Jesus' warnings about his death and rising
decisions.reason: Jesus told his disciples while still in Galilee that the Son of Man would suffer, be killed and be raised on the third day (9:22, 9:44), and said it again on the way to Jerusalem (18:31-33). The women from Galilee were among his followers (8:1-3; 23:55), so they too had heard it.

decisions.choice: must: what had to happen by God's purpose
decisions.reason: The word is the one Jesus used in 9:22 and uses again in 24:26 and 24:44: the suffering and rising are what God planned and the Scriptures foretold.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: As in 9:22, the title is Jesus' way of speaking about himself and his mission.

decisions.choice: sinful people: those who do not follow God's law
decisions.reason: The phrase may point to the Gentiles who carried out the execution, but it covers all who handed Jesus over and put him to death (18:32; 24:20).

decisions.choice: people as the default, men as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, so it follows the gender setting, as 9:44 does.

decisions.choice: Jesus' words quoted directly
decisions.reason: Readable turns the reported words into a quotation, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: They will nail him to a cross
decisions.reason: Readable explains what crucifixion was.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre
decisions.reason: The title chosen for the Gospels, with a capital on both nouns, as Jesus's own name for himself (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: {{gender:personas pecadoras|hombres pecadores}} (L, B); {{gender:gente pecadora|hombres pecadores}} (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the Greek word means human beings (meaning decision m4), and Spanish has two ways to say it, so the gender setting chooses. The adjective agrees with the noun, so the span takes in the whole phrase.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The title chosen for the Gospels, Jesus's own name for himself (meaning decision m3). "Adamu" also means humankind, so it keeps the sense of the Greek.

decisions.choice: watu wenye dhambi, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English sets "people" against "men" under the gender setting. "Watu" already means men and women (meaning decision m4); "wanaume" would mean males only and change the meaning, so Swahili has no span.

decisions.choice: "những người tội lỗi" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "người" already includes men and women, and Vietnamese has no second form to offer, so the English gender setting has no counterpart (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: "Con Người" repeated in the quoted words (R)
decisions.reason: Readable quotes Jesus directly; he speaks of himself as the Son of Man, so Vietnamese repeats the title rather than put "Ngài" in his own mouth. "nộp" as in 23:25.

decisions.choice: "인자"; "넘겨지다"; "사흘째 되는 날에 살아나다", as in the Korean Luke 9:22 and 9:44
decisions.reason: The angels recall Jesus' own predictions (meaning decision), so Korean repeats their words.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "죄인인 사람들" (L), "죄인들" (B, R)
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" and "죄인" already include women and men, so there is no second wording for the setting to offer (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: "ኃጢአተኞች ሰዎች" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "people" or "men" for this word; Amharic "ሰዎች" already means human beings, men and women, and is the plain word for what the Greek says, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

source.text: καὶ ἐμνήσθησαν τῶν ῥημάτων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὑποστρέψασαι ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἕνδεκα καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς λοιποῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And they remembered the words of him, \v 9 and having returned from the tomb they told these things all to the eleven and to all the rest.

en.L: And they remembered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words, \v 9 and having returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words came back to them. \v 9 They went back from the tomb and reported all of this to the Eleven and to everyone else.
en.R: Then the women remembered what Jesus had said. \v 9 They left the tomb and went back to the city. They told the eleven apostles and all the other followers of Jesus about everything that had happened.

es.L: Y se acordaron de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} palabras, \v 9 y, habiendo vuelto del sepulcro, anunciaron todas estas cosas a los once y a todos los demás.
es.B: Entonces recordaron {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} palabras. \v 9 Volvieron del sepulcro y contaron todo esto a los Once y a todos los demás.
es.R: Entonces las mujeres recordaron lo que Jesús había dicho. \v 9 Salieron de la tumba y volvieron a la ciudad. Les contaron todo lo que había pasado a los once apóstoles y a todos los demás discípulos de Jesús.

fr.L: Et elles se souvinrent de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paroles, \v 9 et, revenues du tombeau, elles rapportèrent toutes ces choses aux onze et à tous les autres.
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paroles leur revinrent en mémoire. \v 9 Elles quittèrent le tombeau et allèrent annoncer tout cela aux Onze et à tous les autres.
fr.R: Alors les femmes se sont souvenues de ce que Jésus avait dit. \v 9 Elles ont quitté le tombeau et sont retournées en ville. Elles ont raconté tout ce qui s’était passé aux onze apôtres et à tous les autres qui suivaient Jésus.

sw.L: Nao wakayakumbuka maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \v 9 na waliporudi kutoka kaburini, wakawapasha habari hizi zote wale kumi na mmoja na wengine wote.
sw.B: Ndipo walipoyakumbuka maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \v 9 Walirudi kutoka kaburini, wakawaeleza wale Kumi na Mmoja na wengine wote mambo hayo yote.
sw.R: Ndipo wale wanawake walipokumbuka maneno ya Yesu. \v 9 Waliondoka kaburini, wakarudi mjini. Wakawaambia mitume kumi na mmoja na wanafunzi wengine wote wa Yesu mambo yote yaliyotokea.

vi.L: Và họ nhớ lại những lời của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 9 rồi từ mộ trở về, họ thuật lại tất cả những điều này cho [nhóm] Mười Một và cho tất cả những người khác.
vi.B: Bấy giờ các bà nhớ lại những lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói. \v 9 Rời khỏi mộ, họ trở về và thuật lại mọi điều ấy cho nhóm Mười Một và cho tất cả những người còn lại.
vi.R: Bấy giờ các bà nhớ lại những gì Đức Giê-xu đã nói. \v 9 Họ rời khỏi mộ và trở về thành. Họ kể lại mọi việc đã xảy ra cho mười một sứ đồ và cho tất cả những người khác đi theo Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그러자 그들은 그분의 말씀들을 기억하고, \v 9 무덤에서 돌아와 이 모든 일을 열한 [제자]와 나머지 모든 사람에게 알렸다.
ko.B: 그제야 여자들은 예수의 말씀이 생각났다. \v 9 그들은 무덤에서 돌아와서 이 모든 일을 열한 제자와 다른 모든 사람에게 알렸다.
ko.R: 그러자 여자들은 예수께서 하신 말씀이 생각났다. \v 9 그들은 무덤을 떠나 성안으로 돌아갔다. 그리고 열한 제자와 예수를 따르던 다른 모든 사람에게 그동안 있었던 일을 모두 알렸다.

pt.L: E elas se lembraram das {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} palavras \v 9 e, voltando do sepulcro, anunciaram todas estas coisas aos Onze e a todos os demais.
pt.B: Então elas se lembraram das palavras {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. \v 9 Voltaram do sepulcro e contaram tudo isso aos Onze e a todos os outros.
pt.R: Então as mulheres se lembraram do que Jesus tinha dito. \v 9 Elas saíram do túmulo e voltaram para a cidade. Contaram aos onze apóstolos e a todos os outros seguidores de Jesus tudo o que tinha acontecido.

am.L: ቃሉንም አስታወሱ፤ \v 9 ከመቃብሩም ተመልሰው ይህን ሁሉ ለአሥራ አንዱና ለሌሎቹ ሁሉ ነገሩ።
am.B: ከዚያም ቃሉን አስታወሱ። \v 9 ከመቃብሩ ተመልሰው ይህን ሁሉ ለአሥራ አንዱና ለሌሎቹ ሁሉ ነገሩ።
am.R: ከዚያም ሴቶቹ ኢየሱስ የተናገረውን አስታወሱ። \v 9 ከመቃብሩ ተነሥተው ወደ ከተማ ተመለሱ። የሆነውን ሁሉ ለአሥራ አንዱ ሐዋርያትና ለሌሎቹ የኢየሱስ ደቀ መዛሙርት ሁሉ ነገሩ።

decisions.choice: remembered his words: now understood what he had said
decisions.reason: The disciples had not understood the warnings when they first heard them (9:45; 18:34). Now the women remember them and see what they meant.

decisions.choice: the eleven: the Twelve without Judas
decisions.reason: Judas had betrayed Jesus (22:3-6, 47-48), so the apostles were now eleven. Luke tells of the choice of a twelfth in Acts 1:15-26.

decisions.choice: all the rest: the wider group of disciples
decisions.reason: Other followers were with the apostles, among them the two who set out for Emmaus (24:13, 33).

decisions.choice: went back to the city
decisions.reason: Readable says where they went; the apostles were in Jerusalem (24:33).

decisions.choice: the Eleven (B); the eleven apostles (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced capitalizes the group's name, as with "the Twelve" (9:1); Readable says who they were.

decisions.choice: los once (L); los Once (B); los once apóstoles (R)
decisions.reason: As the term for "the Twelve": Balanced writes the group's name with a capital, Readable says who they are (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: los demás discípulos de Jesús
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers"; Spanish keeps "discípulos" at every level, the term chosen for the Gospels (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: wale kumi na mmoja (L); wale Kumi na Mmoja (B); mitume kumi na mmoja (R)
decisions.reason: As the term for "the Twelve": Balanced writes the group's name with capitals, Readable says who they are (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: wanafunzi wengine wote wa Yesu
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers"; Swahili keeps "wanafunzi" at every level, the term chosen for the Gospels (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "[nhóm] Mười Một" (L); "nhóm Mười Một" (B); "mười một sứ đồ" (R)
decisions.reason: Built like the settled "[nhóm] Mười Hai" / "nhóm Mười Hai" for the Twelve: Vietnamese needs a noun with the number. Readable says "apostles", as the English Readable and the Vietnamese Mark 16:14 do.

decisions.choice: "열한 [제자]" (L); "열한 제자" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 16:14: Korean cannot use the bare number as a noun, and the book's word for disciples is kept rather than the English Readable's "apostles"; Luke names them apostles himself in 24:10.

decisions.choice: os Onze
decisions.reason: The apostles as a group, the Twelve without Judas (m2). Portuguese capitalises "os Doze" at every level (style section 11), so Literal and Balanced write "os Onze" the same way; Readable says "os onze apóstolos", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ለሌሎቹ የኢየሱስ ደቀ መዛሙርት ሁሉ" (to all the other disciples of Jesus) (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the wider group as the English Readable does, but with "ደቀ መዛሙርት", the word for disciples kept at every level in this translation; so also "two of Jesus' disciples" in 24:13.

source.text: ἦσαν δὲ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία καὶ Ἰωάννα καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ σὺν αὐταῖς· ἔλεγον πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ταῦτα.

records.literal_gloss: Were now the Magdalene Mary and Joanna and Mary the [mother] of James and the rest with them; they were telling to the apostles these things.

en.L: Now they were Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the [mother] of James, and the rest [of the women] with them; they were telling these things to the apostles.
en.B: The women were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the others who were with them. They kept telling the apostles about these things.
en.R: The women who told the apostles these things were Mary from the town of Magdala, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and some other women who were with them.

es.L: Y eran María la Magdalena, y Juana, y María la [madre] de Santiago, y las demás [mujeres] con ellas; decían estas cosas a los apóstoles.
es.B: Eran María Magdalena, Juana, María la madre de Santiago y las demás mujeres que estaban con ellas. Y no dejaban de contar estas cosas a los apóstoles.
es.R: Las mujeres que contaron estas cosas a los apóstoles fueron María, la del pueblo de Magdala, Juana, María la madre de Santiago y otras mujeres que estaban con ellas.

fr.L: Or c’étaient Marie la Magdaléenne, et Jeanne, et Marie, [la mère] de Jacques, et les autres [femmes] avec elles ; elles disaient ces choses aux apôtres.
fr.B: C’étaient Marie de Magdala, Jeanne, Marie, mère de Jacques, et les autres femmes qui étaient avec elles. Elles ne cessaient de raconter cela aux apôtres.
fr.R: Les femmes qui ont raconté tout cela aux apôtres étaient Marie, de la ville de Magdala, Jeanne, Marie, la mère de Jacques, et d’autres femmes qui étaient avec elles.

sw.L: Basi walikuwa Mariamu Magdalene, na Yoana, na Mariamu [mama] wa Yakobo, na [wanawake] wengine pamoja nao; walikuwa wakiwaambia mitume mambo haya.
sw.B: Wanawake hao walikuwa Mariamu Magdalene, Yoana, Mariamu mama yake Yakobo, na wengine waliokuwa pamoja nao. Hao ndio walioendelea kuwaeleza mitume mambo hayo.
sw.R: Wanawake waliowaambia mitume mambo haya ni Mariamu wa mji wa Magdala, Yoana, Mariamu mama yake Yakobo, na wanawake wengine waliokuwa pamoja nao.

vi.L: Đó là Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len, Gian-nơ, Ma-ri [mẹ] của Gia-cơ, và những người [phụ nữ] khác cùng với họ; họ cứ kể những điều này cho các sứ đồ.
vi.B: Những người phụ nữ ấy là Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len, Gian-nơ, Ma-ri mẹ của Gia-cơ, và những người khác cùng đi với họ. Họ cứ kể đi kể lại những điều ấy cho các sứ đồ.
vi.R: Những người phụ nữ kể lại các việc này cho các sứ đồ là Ma-ri, người làng Ma-đơ-la, Gian-nơ, Ma-ri mẹ của Gia-cơ, và mấy người phụ nữ khác đi cùng với họ.

ko.L: 그런데 [그 여자들은] 막달라 마리아와 요안나와 야고보의 [어머니] 마리아와, 그들과 함께 있던 다른 [여자들]이었다. 이들이 이 일들을 사도들에게 말하고 있었다.
ko.B: 그 여자들은 막달라 마리아와 요안나와 야고보의 어머니 마리아, 그리고 그들과 함께 있던 다른 여자들이었다. 이 여자들이 사도들에게 이 일들을 거듭 전했다.
ko.R: 사도들에게 이 일을 알린 여자들은 막달라라는 마을에서 온 마리아, 요안나, 야고보의 어머니 마리아, 그리고 그들과 함께 있던 다른 여자들이었다.

pt.L: E eram Maria Madalena, e Joana, e Maria, a [mãe] de Tiago, e as demais [mulheres] com elas; elas diziam estas coisas aos apóstolos.
pt.B: As mulheres eram Maria Madalena, Joana, Maria, mãe de Tiago, e as outras que estavam com elas. Elas contavam essas coisas aos apóstolos.
pt.R: As mulheres que contaram essas coisas aos apóstolos foram Maria, da cidade de Magdala, Joana, Maria, a mãe de Tiago, e algumas outras mulheres que estavam com elas.

am.L: እነርሱም መግደላዊት ማርያም፣ ዮሐና፣ የያዕቆብ [እናት] ማርያምና ከእነርሱ ጋር የነበሩት ሌሎቹ [ሴቶች] ነበሩ፤ ይህንንም ለሐዋርያት ይነግሩ ነበር።
am.B: ሴቶቹም መግደላዊት ማርያም፣ ዮሐና፣ የያዕቆብ እናት ማርያምና ከእነርሱ ጋር የነበሩት ሌሎቹ ሴቶች ነበሩ። እነርሱም ይህን ለሐዋርያት ደጋግመው ይነግሩ ነበር።
am.R: ይህን ለሐዋርያት የነገሩት ሴቶች ከመቅደላ ከተማ የሆነችው ማርያም፣ ዮሐና፣ የያዕቆብ እናት ማርያምና ከእነርሱ ጋር የነበሩ ሌሎች ሴቶች ነበሩ።

decisions.choice: Mary Magdalene and Joanna: women who had followed Jesus from Galilee
decisions.reason: Luke has named them before: Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out, and Joanna the wife of Chuza, a manager in Herod's household (8:2-3). They provided for Jesus and the Twelve from their own means.

decisions.choice: Mary the mother of James
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "Mary of James", a common way of naming a woman by a family member. Mark 15:40 and 16:1 call her the mother of James, so "mother" is supplied.

decisions.choice: were telling: told again and again
decisions.reason: The verb is in the imperfect tense: the women kept telling the apostles, who would not believe them (24:11).

decisions.choice: the women are the first witnesses
alternatives: the apostles are the first witnesses
decisions.reason: Luke names the women as the first to hear that Jesus had been raised and the first to tell it, though the testimony of women was often given little weight at the time.

decisions.choice: one sentence that names the women who told the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable joins the list and the telling, which is how the two clauses relate.

decisions.choice: Mary from the town of Magdala
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name: Magdala was a town on the Lake of Galilee, as at 8:2.

decisions.choice: no dejaban de contar
decisions.reason: The imperfect says they told it again and again (meaning decision m3); Balanced says so in words, as the English "kept telling" does.

decisions.choice: "Gian-nơ"; "Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len" (L, B), "Ma-ri, người làng Ma-đơ-la" (R)
decisions.reason: "Gian-nơ" as in the Vietnamese Luke 8:3; Readable explains Mary's byname as in the Vietnamese Mark 15:40.

decisions.choice: "막달라 마리아", "요안나", "야고보의 [어머니] 마리아"; "사도들" at every level
decisions.reason: The forms of the Korean Mark 15:40 and Luke 8:3; Luke uses his word for the apostles here, as in Luke 6:13.

source.text: καὶ ἐφάνησαν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λῆρος τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα, καὶ ἠπίστουν αὐταῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And appeared before them like nonsense the words these, and they were disbelieving them.

en.L: And these words appeared before them like nonsense, and they did not believe them.
en.B: But to the apostles the report sounded like nonsense, and they would not believe the women.
en.R: But the apostles thought the women's story was foolish talk. They would not believe them.

es.L: Y estas palabras les parecieron a ellos como un disparate, y no les creían.
es.B: Pero a los apóstoles aquel relato les pareció un disparate, y no quisieron creer a las mujeres.
es.R: Pero los apóstoles pensaron que lo que decían las mujeres eran tonterías. No les quisieron creer.

fr.L: Et ces paroles parurent à leurs yeux comme du délire, et ils ne les croyaient pas.
fr.B: Mais ce récit parut aux apôtres n’être que du délire, et ils refusaient de croire les femmes.
fr.R: Mais les apôtres ont pensé que l’histoire des femmes était absurde. Ils refusaient de les croire.

sw.L: Na maneno haya yalionekana mbele yao kama upuuzi, nao hawakuwaamini.
sw.B: Lakini kwa mitume, habari hiyo ilionekana kama upuuzi, wakakataa kuwaamini wale wanawake.
sw.R: Lakini mitume waliona kwamba habari za wale wanawake ni maneno ya kipuuzi. Hawakutaka kuwaamini.

vi.L: Nhưng trước mắt họ những lời ấy dường như chuyện nhảm, và họ không tin các bà.
vi.B: Nhưng các sứ đồ cho rằng những lời ấy là chuyện vô lý, nên không chịu tin các bà.
vi.R: Nhưng các sứ đồ nghĩ rằng chuyện các bà kể là chuyện vớ vẩn. Họ không chịu tin các bà.

ko.L: 그런데 이 말들이 그들에게는 헛소리처럼 보였고, 그들은 그 여자들을 믿지 않았다.
ko.B: 그러나 사도들에게는 이 말이 헛소리처럼 들렸다. 그래서 그들은 여자들의 말을 믿지 않았다.
ko.R: 그러나 사도들은 여자들의 이야기가 터무니없는 말이라고 생각했다. 그래서 여자들의 말을 믿으려 하지 않았다.

pt.L: E essas palavras pareceram diante deles como um delírio, e não criam nelas.
pt.B: Mas para os apóstolos o relato pareceu um absurdo, e eles não quiseram crer nas mulheres.
pt.R: Mas os apóstolos acharam que a história das mulheres era bobagem. Eles não quiseram acreditar nelas.

am.L: ይህም ቃል በፊታቸው እንደ ከንቱ ወሬ ታየ፤ አላመኑአቸውምም።
am.B: ሐዋርያት ግን ወሬው ከንቱ ንግግር መሰላቸው፤ ሴቶቹንም አላመኑአቸውም።
am.R: ሐዋርያት ግን የሴቶቹ ወሬ የሞኝ ንግግር መሰላቸው። ስለዚህ አላመኑአቸውም።

decisions.choice: nonsense: idle talk, wild stories
decisions.reason: The word is used for empty chatter or the talk of someone who is not in their right mind. The apostles do not think the women are lying, only that their story cannot be true.

decisions.choice: they did not believe: they went on refusing to believe
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes continuing unbelief. The theme of slowness to believe runs through the chapter (24:25, 38, 41).

decisions.choice: the apostles ... the women
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is meant by each "them".

decisions.choice: du délire (L, B); absurde (R)
decisions.reason: The word is idle or wild talk (m1). "Sornettes" and "balivernes" sound quaint, and "radotage" suggests an old person repeating himself; "du délire" is the current word for talk that makes no sense, and it says as strongly as the Greek how the report was received.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἀναστὰς ἔδραμεν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει τὰ ὀθόνια μόνα· καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὑτὸν θαυμάζων τὸ γεγονός.

records.literal_gloss: But Peter having risen up ran to the tomb, and having stooped down he sees the linen cloths alone, and he went away to himself wondering at that having happened.

en.L: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb; and stooping to look in, he sees the linen cloths alone; and he went away to his home, marveling at what had happened.
en.B: Peter, though, got up and ran to the tomb. He bent down to look in and saw nothing but the linen wrappings. Then he went home, amazed at what had taken place.
en.R: But Peter jumped up and ran to the tomb. He bent down and looked inside. All he saw were the strips of linen cloth that had been wrapped around the body. Then he went home, amazed and wondering what had happened.

es.L: Pero Pedro, levantándose, corrió al sepulcro; e inclinándose [para mirar dentro], ve los lienzos de lino solos; y se fue a su casa, asombrado de lo que había sucedido.
es.B: Pedro, sin embargo, se levantó y fue corriendo al sepulcro. Se agachó para mirar dentro y no vio más que los lienzos de lino. Luego se volvió a su casa, asombrado por lo que había pasado.
es.R: Pero Pedro se levantó de un salto y corrió a la tumba. Se agachó y miró dentro. Solo vio las tiras de lino con que habían envuelto el cuerpo. Después se fue a su casa, asombrado y preguntándose qué había pasado.

fr.L: Mais Pierre, s’étant levé, courut au tombeau ; et, se penchant, il voit les linges seuls ; et il s’en alla chez lui, s’étonnant de ce qui était arrivé.
fr.B: Pierre, cependant, se leva et courut au tombeau. Il se pencha pour regarder à l’intérieur et ne vit que les bandes de lin. Puis il rentra chez lui, étonné de ce qui s’était passé.
fr.R: Mais Pierre s’est levé d’un bond et a couru au tombeau. Il s’est penché et a regardé à l’intérieur. Il a vu seulement les bandes de tissu qu’on avait enroulées autour du corps. Puis il est rentré chez lui. Il était étonné et se demandait ce qui s’était passé.

sw.L: Lakini Petro akainuka, akakimbia kaburini; na akiinama [kuchungulia ndani], anaona vitambaa vya kitani peke yake; naye akaenda zake nyumbani, akiyastaajabia yaliyotokea.
sw.B: Lakini Petro aliinuka, akakimbia kaburini. Akainama kuchungulia ndani, akaona vitambaa vya kitani tu. Kisha akarudi nyumbani, akistaajabu kwa yale yaliyotokea.
sw.R: Lakini Petro aliinuka haraka, akakimbia kaburini. Aliinama, akachungulia ndani. Aliona tu vitambaa vya kitani vilivyokuwa vimezungushiwa mwili. Kisha akarudi nyumbani, akishangaa na kujiuliza ni nini kilichotokea.

vi.L: Nhưng Phi-e-rơ đứng dậy chạy đến mộ; và cúi xuống nhìn vào, ông thấy chỉ có những dải vải gai mà thôi; rồi ông trở về nhà, ngạc nhiên về việc đã xảy ra.
vi.B: Tuy vậy, Phi-e-rơ đứng dậy và chạy đến mộ. Ông cúi xuống nhìn vào, và chỉ thấy những dải vải gai. Rồi ông về nhà, lấy làm lạ về điều đã xảy ra.
vi.R: Nhưng Phi-e-rơ vùng dậy và chạy đến mộ. Ông cúi xuống nhìn vào trong. Ông chỉ thấy những dải vải gai đã từng quấn quanh thi thể. Rồi ông về nhà, vừa ngạc nhiên vừa thắc mắc không biết chuyện gì đã xảy ra.

ko.L: 그러나 베드로는 일어나 무덤으로 달려갔다. 그리고 몸을 굽혀 들여다보고, 베 천들만 [놓여 있는 것을] 본다. 그리고 그는 일어난 일을 이상히 여기며 자기 집으로 돌아갔다.
ko.B: 그러나 베드로는 일어나 무덤으로 달려갔다. 몸을 굽혀 안을 들여다보니 고운 베만 놓여 있었다. 베드로는 일어난 일을 이상히 여기며 집으로 돌아갔다.
ko.R: 그러나 베드로는 벌떡 일어나 무덤으로 달려갔다. 그는 몸을 굽혀 안을 들여다보았다. 시신을 감쌌던 고운 베 천만 놓여 있었다. 베드로는 어떻게 된 일인지 놀라고 궁금해하며 집으로 돌아갔다.

pt.L: Mas Pedro, levantando-se, correu ao sepulcro; e, abaixando-se para olhar, vê só as faixas de linho; e foi embora para casa, admirado com o que tinha acontecido.
pt.B: Pedro, porém, se levantou e correu ao sepulcro. Ele se abaixou para olhar e viu apenas as faixas de linho. Depois voltou para casa, admirado com o que tinha acontecido.
pt.R: Mas Pedro se levantou depressa e correu até o túmulo. Ele se abaixou e olhou lá dentro. Só viu as faixas de pano de linho que tinham envolvido o corpo. Depois foi para casa, admirado e pensando no que tinha acontecido.

am.L: ጴጥሮስ ግን ተነሥቶ ወደ መቃብሩ ሮጠ፤ ጎንበስ ብሎም የበፍታ ጨርቆቹን ብቻ ያያል፤ በሆነውም ነገር እየተደነቀ ወደ ቤቱ ሄደ።
am.B: ጴጥሮስ ግን ተነሥቶ ወደ መቃብሩ ሮጠ። ጎንበስ ብሎ ወደ ውስጥ ሲመለከት ከበፍታ ጨርቆቹ በቀር ምንም አላየም። ከዚያም በሆነው ነገር እየተደነቀ ወደ ቤቱ ሄደ።
am.R: ጴጥሮስ ግን ብድግ ብሎ ወደ መቃብሩ ሮጠ። ጎንበስ ብሎ ወደ ውስጥ ተመለከተ። ያየው በአስከሬኑ ላይ ተጠቅልለው የነበሩትን የበፍታ ጨርቆች ብቻ ነበር። ከዚያም ተደንቆ ምን እንደ ሆነ እያሰበ ወደ ቤቱ ሄደ።

decisions.choice: the verse is included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse is left out, as in Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 among them, have the verse. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts lack it. Some think it was added from John 20:3-10, which tells of Peter and another disciple at the tomb; but the visit to the tomb is mentioned again in 24:24. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he sees: a vivid present in the middle of a past account
decisions.reason: Luke switches to the present tense to put the reader beside Peter at the moment he looks in.

decisions.choice: the linen cloths alone: the burial wrappings, with no body in them
decisions.reason: The word is for strips or pieces of linen used to wrap a body (John 19:40). That they lay there "alone" shows that the body had not been carried off in its wrappings.

decisions.choice: went away to his home
decisions.reason: The phrase is "to himself". It most likely means to where he was staying (John 20:10 has a similar phrase). Some join it to the next word: "wondering to himself".

decisions.choice: that had been wrapped around the body
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the cloths were.

decisions.choice: saw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the past tense of the story.

decisions.choice: ve (L); vio (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke changes to the present in the middle of a past account (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does.

decisions.choice: lienzos de lino
decisions.reason: The same words as for the burial wrappings in John 19:40 and 20:5 (meaning decision m3). Readable, like the English, says they were strips that had been wrapped around the body.

decisions.choice: les linges (L); les bandes de lin (B); les bandes de tissu qu’on avait enroulées autour du corps (R)
decisions.reason: The word is strips or pieces of linen used to wrap the body (m3). "Bandelettes" makes French readers think of Egyptian mummies; "les linges" is the plain word at Literal, and Balanced and Readable say what the cloths were.

decisions.choice: anaona (L); akaona, aliona (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke changes to the present in the middle of a past account (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it; Balanced uses -ka- for the verbs that follow in the sequence, and Readable the plain past.

decisions.choice: vitambaa vya kitani
decisions.reason: The same words as for the burial wrappings in John 19:40 and 20:5 (meaning decision m3); "sanda" is a single sheet, which the word does not say.

decisions.choice: "ông thấy" (L) with no past marker
decisions.reason: Luke's vivid present "he sees" (meaning decision) is shown, as far as Vietnamese can, by leaving out "đã", as the Vietnamese Mark does with the historic present.

decisions.choice: "những dải vải gai"
decisions.reason: The burial wrappings, as in John 19:40 and 20:5.

decisions.choice: Historic present "본다" (L), past (B, R); "베 천들" (L), "고운 베" (B), "고운 베 천" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Luke's vivid present (meaning decision), as the Korean Mark does; the cloth words are those of the Korean John 20:5-7 for the same wrappings.

source.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἦσαν πορευόμενοι εἰς κώμην ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ᾗ ὄνομα Ἐμμαοῦς, καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡμίλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους περὶ πάντων τῶν συμβεβηκότων τούτων.

records.literal_gloss: And behold two of them on same the day were going to a village being distant stadia sixty from Jerusalem, whose name [was] Emmaus, \v 14 and they were talking with one another about all these things having happened.

en.L: And look, on that same day two of them were going to a village sixty stadia distant from Jerusalem, whose name [was] Emmaus, \v 14 and they were talking with one another about all these things that had happened.
en.B: On that very day two of them were walking to Emmaus, a village {{units:about seven miles|sixty stadia}} from Jerusalem. \v 14 They were deep in conversation about all that had happened.
en.R: That same day two of Jesus' followers were walking to a village called Emmaus. It was {{units:about seven miles|sixty stadia}} from Jerusalem. \v 14 On the way they talked with each other about all these events.

es.L: Y mira, ese mismo día dos de ellos iban a una aldea que distaba sesenta estadios de Jerusalén, cuyo nombre [era] Emaús, \v 14 y ellos conversaban entre sí de todas estas cosas que habían sucedido.
es.B: Ese mismo día, dos de ellos iban de camino a Emaús, una aldea a {{units:unos once kilómetros|sesenta estadios}} de Jerusalén. \v 14 Iban conversando a fondo sobre todo lo que había ocurrido.
es.R: Ese mismo día, dos de los discípulos de Jesús iban caminando a una aldea llamada Emaús. Estaba a {{units:unos once kilómetros|sesenta estadios}} de Jerusalén. \v 14 Por el camino hablaban entre ellos de todo lo que había pasado.

fr.L: Et voici, ce même jour, deux d’entre eux se rendaient à un village distant de soixante stades de Jérusalem, dont le nom [était] Emmaüs, \v 14 et ils s’entretenaient l’un avec l’autre de toutes ces choses qui étaient arrivées.
fr.B: Ce même jour, deux d’entre eux se rendaient à Emmaüs, un village situé à {{units:environ 11 kilomètres|soixante stades}} de Jérusalem. \v 14 Ils discutaient longuement de tout ce qui était arrivé.
fr.R: Ce jour-là, deux disciples de Jésus marchaient vers un village appelé Emmaüs. Il était à {{units:environ 11 kilomètres|soixante stades}} de Jérusalem. \v 14 En chemin, ils parlaient ensemble de tout ce qui s’était passé.

sw.L: Na tazama, siku ile ile wawili wao walikuwa wakienda kijiji kimoja kilichokuwa umbali wa stadia sitini kutoka Yerusalemu, jina lake Emau, \v 14 nao walikuwa wakizungumza wao kwa wao juu ya mambo hayo yote yaliyotokea.
sw.B: Siku hiyo hiyo wawili wao walikuwa wakienda Emau, kijiji kilichokuwa {{units:kama kilomita kumi na moja|stadia sitini}} kutoka Yerusalemu. \v 14 Walikuwa wakizungumza kwa makini juu ya yote yaliyotokea.
sw.R: Siku hiyo hiyo, wanafunzi wawili wa Yesu walikuwa wakitembea kwenda kijiji kimoja kiitwacho Emau. Kilikuwa {{units:kama kilomita kumi na moja|stadia sitini}} kutoka Yerusalemu. \v 14 Njiani walikuwa wakizungumza wao kwa wao juu ya mambo hayo yote.

vi.L: Và kìa, ngay trong ngày ấy, có hai người trong số họ đang đi đến một làng cách Giê-ru-sa-lem sáu mươi ếch-ta-đơ, tên là Em-ma-út, \v 14 và họ trò chuyện với nhau về tất cả những việc đã xảy ra.
vi.B: Cũng trong ngày hôm ấy, có hai người trong số họ đang đi đến Em-ma-út, một làng cách Giê-ru-sa-lem {{units:khoảng 11 km|sáu mươi ếch-ta-đơ}}. \v 14 Họ đang mải trò chuyện với nhau về mọi việc đã xảy ra.
vi.R: Cũng ngày hôm ấy, có hai người trong số những người theo Đức Giê-xu đang đi đến một làng tên là Em-ma-út. Làng ấy cách Giê-ru-sa-lem {{units:khoảng 11 km|sáu mươi ếch-ta-đơ}}. \v 14 Dọc đường họ trò chuyện với nhau về tất cả những việc ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 보라, 바로 그날 그들 가운데 두 사람이 예루살렘에서 육십 스타디온 떨어진 마을로 가고 있었는데, 그 마을의 이름은 엠마오였다. \v 14 그리고 그들은 일어난 이 모든 일에 관하여 서로 이야기하고 있었다.
ko.B: 바로 그날 그들 가운데 두 사람이 예루살렘에서 {{units:약 11킬로미터|육십 스타디온}} 떨어진 엠마오라는 마을로 가고 있었다. \v 14 그들은 그동안 일어난 모든 일에 관하여 서로 이야기를 나누고 있었다.
ko.R: 그날 예수를 따르던 사람들 가운데 두 사람이 엠마오라는 마을로 걸어가고 있었다. 그 마을은 예루살렘에서 {{units:약 11킬로미터|육십 스타디온}} 떨어져 있었다. \v 14 그들은 가면서 그동안 있었던 모든 일에 관하여 서로 이야기했다.

pt.L: E eis que, naquele mesmo dia, dois deles iam para um povoado distante sessenta estádios de Jerusalém, cujo nome [era] Emaús, \v 14 e eles conversavam entre si sobre todas essas coisas que tinham acontecido.
pt.B: Naquele mesmo dia, dois deles estavam indo para Emaús, um povoado a {{units:cerca de onze quilômetros|sessenta estádios}} de Jerusalém. \v 14 Iam conversando sobre tudo o que tinha acontecido.
pt.R: Naquele mesmo dia, dois seguidores de Jesus estavam indo a pé para um povoado chamado Emaús. Ficava a {{units:cerca de onze quilômetros|sessenta estádios}} de Jerusalém. \v 14 No caminho, eles conversavam sobre tudo o que tinha acontecido.

am.L: እነሆም፣ ከእነርሱ ሁለቱ በዚያው ቀን ከኢየሩሳሌም 60 ምዕራፍ ርቃ ወደምትገኝ መንደር ይሄዱ ነበር፤ ስሟም ኤማሁስ [ነበረ]፤ \v 14 እነርሱም ስለ ሆነው ስለዚህ ሁሉ እርስ በርሳቸው ይነጋገሩ ነበር።
am.B: በዚያው ቀን ከእነርሱ ሁለቱ ከኢየሩሳሌም {{units:11 ኪሎ ሜትር ያህል|60 ምዕራፍ}} ርቃ ወደምትገኘው ኤማሁስ ወደምትባል መንደር እየሄዱ ነበር። \v 14 ስለ ሆነው ነገር ሁሉ በጥልቀት ይነጋገሩ ነበር።
am.R: በዚያው ቀን ከኢየሱስ ደቀ መዛሙርት ሁለቱ ኤማሁስ ወደምትባል መንደር እየሄዱ ነበር። መንደሯ ከኢየሩሳሌም {{units:11 ኪሎ ሜትር ያህል|60 ምዕራፍ}} ትርቅ ነበር። \v 14 በመንገድም ስለ ሆነው ነገር ሁሉ እርስ በርሳቸው ይነጋገሩ ነበር።

decisions.choice: two of them: two of the wider group of disciples, not of the eleven
decisions.reason: "Them" points back to "all the rest" with the eleven (24:9). When the two return, they find "the eleven and those with them" (24:33). One is named Cleopas (24:18).

decisions.choice: sixty stadia: about seven miles (11 kilometers)
decisions.reason: A stadion was a Greek measure of about 607 feet (185 meters). Sixty of them make a walk of two or three hours.

decisions.choice: sixty: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: a hundred and sixty, the reading of Codex Sinaiticus and some other manuscripts
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read sixty. Codex Sinaiticus and a few others read a hundred and sixty, which would fit a town called Emmaus about 19 miles from Jerusalem but would make the return the same evening (24:33) very hard. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Emmaus: a village whose location is no longer certain
decisions.reason: Several places have been suggested. Luke gives only the distance from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to begin a new scene. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: about seven miles as the default, sixty stadia as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the distance in modern measure; the Measures setting shows the original unit. Literal keeps the unit of the Greek.

decisions.choice: Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" refers to.

decisions.choice: {{units:unos once kilómetros|sesenta estadios}}
decisions.reason: Spanish readers measure in kilometres, so the default is metric, as in John 6:19, where the English default is miles; sixty stadia is about 11 kilometres (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the Greek measure.

decisions.choice: dos de los discípulos de Jesús
alternatives: dos de los seguidores de Jesús
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers"; Spanish keeps "discípulos" at every level. They are from the wider group, not the eleven (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 11 kilomètres|soixante stades}} (B, R); soixante stades (L)
decisions.reason: French readers measure distance in kilometres, so the default is metric rather than the English miles; sixty stadia were about 11 kilometres (m2). The Measures setting shows the original unit, and Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: {{units:kama kilomita kumi na moja|stadia sitini}}
decisions.reason: Swahili readers measure in kilometres, so the default is metric, as in John 6:19, where the English default is miles; sixty stadia is about 11 kilometres (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the Greek measure.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi wawili wa Yesu
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "followers"; Swahili keeps "wanafunzi" at every level. They are from the wider group, not the eleven (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: {{units:khoảng 11 km|sáu mươi ếch-ta-đơ}} (B, R); "sáu mươi ếch-ta-đơ" (L)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese uses metric measures by default with the original unit as the alternative (style guide, section 7), unlike the English miles; Literal keeps the original unit.

decisions.choice: "Em-ma-út"
decisions.reason: The hyphenated Protestant transliteration of the village name.

decisions.choice: {{units:약 11킬로미터|육십 스타디온}} (B, R); "육십 스타디온" (L)
alternatives: US miles as the default, as in English
decisions.reason: Korean uses metric as the modern default, unlike the English US miles (style guide, section 7); Literal keeps the original unit. The figure follows the meaning decision (about 11 kilometers).

decisions.choice: cerca de onze quilômetros as the default, sessenta estádios as the alternative
alternatives: about seven miles, as the English
decisions.reason: Portuguese readers measure in kilometres, so the units setting defaults to metric (style section 7), where the English defaults to miles; sixty stadia are about 11 kilometres (m2). Literal keeps "sessenta estádios".

decisions.choice: {{units:11 ኪሎ ሜትር ያህል|60 ምዕራፍ}} (B, R); "60 ምዕራፍ" (L)
alternatives: {{units:7 ማይል ያህል|60 ምዕራፍ}}, the English US default
decisions.reason: Amharic readers measure distance in kilometres, so the modern default is metric, with the Greek unit, "ምዕራፍ" (a stadion, the Amharic Bible word for it), as the alternative; Literal keeps the Greek count.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὁμιλεῖν αὐτοὺς καὶ συζητεῖν καὶ αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς ἐγγίσας συνεπορεύετο αὐτοῖς, οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἐκρατοῦντο τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the talking them and discussing that himself Jesus having drawn near was walking along with them, \v 16 but the eyes of them were held [so as] not to recognize him.

en.L: And it happened, while they were talking and discussing, that Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} drew near and was walking along with them, \v 16 but their eyes were held back from recognizing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: While they were talking it over and debating, Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} came near and began to walk with them. \v 16 But their eyes were held back, and they did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: While they were talking and trying to understand it all, Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} came up and walked along with them. \v 16 But their eyes were kept from knowing who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.

es.L: Y sucedió que, mientras ellos conversaban y discutían, también Jesús mismo, habiéndose acercado, caminaba con ellos, \v 16 pero sus ojos estaban retenidos para que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} reconocieran.
es.B: Mientras conversaban y discutían, Jesús mismo se acercó y se puso a caminar con ellos. \v 16 Pero sus ojos estaban retenidos, de modo que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} reconocieron.
es.R: Mientras hablaban y trataban de entender todo aquello, Jesús mismo se les acercó y caminó con ellos. \v 16 Pero sus ojos fueron retenidos, y no supieron quién era {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Et il arriva, tandis qu’ils s’entretenaient et discutaient, que Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, s’étant approché, faisait route avec eux, \v 16 mais leurs yeux étaient empêchés de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} reconnaître.
fr.B: Pendant qu’ils parlaient et discutaient, Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} s’approcha et se mit à marcher avec eux. \v 16 Mais leurs yeux étaient comme retenus, et ils ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} reconnurent pas.
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils parlaient et essayaient de tout comprendre, Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} est arrivé près d’eux et a marché avec eux. \v 16 Mais quelque chose empêchait leurs yeux de voir qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était.

sw.L: Ikawa, walipokuwa wakizungumza na kujadiliana, Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} akakaribia, akawa akitembea pamoja nao, \v 16 lakini macho yao yalizuiliwa wasimtambue.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakizungumza na kujadiliana, Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aliwakaribia, akaanza kutembea pamoja nao. \v 16 Lakini macho yao yalizuiliwa, wakashindwa kumtambua.
sw.R: Walipokuwa wakizungumza na kujaribu kuelewa mambo hayo yote, Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aliwakaribia, akatembea pamoja nao. \v 16 Lakini macho yao yalizuiliwa wasijue kwamba ni {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.

vi.L: Và xảy ra là, trong khi họ đang trò chuyện và bàn luận, thì chính Đức Giê-xu đến gần và cùng đi với họ, \v 16 nhưng mắt họ bị ngăn lại, không nhận ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Đang khi họ trò chuyện và bàn luận với nhau, thì chính Đức Giê-xu đến gần và cùng đi với họ. \v 16 Nhưng mắt họ bị che khuất nên không nhận ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Trong khi họ đang nói chuyện và cố hiểu mọi việc, chính Đức Giê-xu đến gần và đi cùng với họ. \v 16 Nhưng mắt họ bị ngăn lại, nên họ không nhận ra {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là ai.

ko.L: 그리고 [이런] 일이 있었다. 그들이 이야기하며 토론하고 있을 때에, 예수께서 친히 가까이 오셔서 그들과 함께 걸어가셨다. \v 16 그러나 그들의 눈이 붙들려서 그분을 알아보지 못했다.
ko.B: 그들이 이야기하며 서로 묻고 따지는 동안, 예수께서 몸소 다가오셔서 그들과 함께 걸으셨다. \v 16 그러나 그들은 눈이 가려져서 예수를 알아보지 못했다.
ko.R: 그들이 이야기를 나누며 이 모든 일을 이해해 보려고 애쓰고 있을 때, 예수께서 직접 다가오셔서 그들과 함께 걸으셨다. \v 16 그러나 그들의 눈이 가려져서 그분이 누구신지 알아보지 못했다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, enquanto conversavam e discutiam, o próprio Jesus se aproximou e caminhava com eles, \v 16 mas os olhos deles estavam impedidos de {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} reconhecer.
pt.B: Enquanto conversavam e debatiam, o próprio Jesus se aproximou e começou a caminhar com eles. \v 16 Mas os olhos deles estavam impedidos, e eles não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} reconheceram.
pt.R: Enquanto eles conversavam e tentavam entender tudo aquilo, o próprio Jesus chegou perto e foi andando com eles. \v 16 Mas os olhos deles foram impedidos de reconhecer quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} era.

am.L: እንዲህም ሆነ፤ ሲነጋገሩና ሲመራመሩ ሳሉ ኢየሱስ ራሱ ቀርቦ ከእነርሱ ጋር ይሄድ ነበር፤ \v 16 ዓይኖቻቸው ግን እንዳያውቁት ተይዘው ነበር።
am.B: ሲነጋገሩና ሲከራከሩ ሳሉ ኢየሱስ ራሱ ቀርቦ ከእነርሱ ጋር መጓዝ ጀመረ። \v 16 ዓይኖቻቸው ግን ተይዘው ስለ ነበር አላወቁትም።
am.R: ይህን ሁሉ ለመረዳት እየሞከሩ ሲነጋገሩ ኢየሱስ ራሱ መጥቶ ከእነርሱ ጋር አብሮ ይሄድ ጀመር። \v 16 ዓይኖቻቸው ግን ማን እንደ ሆነ እንዳያውቁ ተከልክለው ነበር።

decisions.choice: discussing: debating, asking each other questions
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or examine together. They are trying to make sense of what has happened.

decisions.choice: their eyes were held back: they were kept from recognizing him
decisions.reason: The passive does not say who held their eyes. The same eyes are "opened" in 24:31, which suggests that God kept them from knowing him until the right moment. The question is left open, and every level keeps the passive.

decisions.choice: Jesus himself came near: the risen Jesus joins his followers
decisions.reason: "Himself" stresses that it was Jesus, though they did not know it. The reader knows more than the two travelers.

decisions.choice: trying to understand it all
decisions.reason: Readable says what their discussion was about.

decisions.choice: Jesús mismo, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English "himself" takes the setting, but Spanish "mismo" after a name is an adjective, not a pronoun, so there is nothing for the setting to capitalise.

decisions.choice: "chính Đức Giê-xu" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Mark 16:8: Vietnamese marks "Jesus himself" with "chính" before the name, with no pronoun.

decisions.choice: "친히" (L), "몸소" (B), "직접" (R) for autos; "눈이 붙들려" (L), "눈이 가려져" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of eyes held back; Balanced and Readable use the natural Korean picture. Neither says why, as the passive leaves it open (meaning decision).

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίνες οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὓς ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους περιπατοῦντες;

records.literal_gloss: He said then to them, What [are] the words these that you are exchanging with one another walking?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "What [are] these words that you are exchanging with one another as you walk?"
en.B: He said to them, "What is this conversation you are having with each other as you walk?"
en.R: Jesus asked them, "What is all this you are saying to each other on the road?"

es.L: Y les dijo: «¿Qué [son] estas palabras que {{plural_you:intercambian|intercambiáis}} uno con otro mientras {{plural_you:caminan|camináis}}?».
es.B: Les preguntó: «¿Qué es eso de lo que {{plural_you:van|vais}} hablando entre los dos por el camino?».
es.R: Jesús les preguntó: «¿De qué {{plural_you:están|estáis}} hablando entre los dos por el camino?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Quelles [sont] ces paroles que vous échangez l’un avec l’autre en marchant ? »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Quelle est cette conversation que vous avez ensemble en chemin ? »
fr.R: Jésus leur a demandé : « De quoi parlez-vous ensemble sur la route ? »

sw.L: Akawaambia, "Ni maneno gani haya mnayobadilishana ninyi kwa ninyi mnapotembea?"
sw.B: Akawauliza, "Ni mazungumzo gani haya mnayofanya njiani mnapotembea?"
sw.R: Yesu akawauliza, "Mnaambiana nini hivyo njiani?"

vi.L: Ngài nói với họ: "Các anh đang trao đổi với nhau những lời gì trong khi đi đường vậy?"
vi.B: Ngài hỏi họ: "Các anh đang bàn chuyện gì với nhau trên đường đi vậy?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi họ: "Các anh đang nói gì với nhau trên đường đi thế?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희가 걸어가면서 서로 주고받는 이 말들은 무엇이냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 물으셨다. "길을 걸으며 서로 주고받는 이야기가 무엇이냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 물으셨다. "길을 가면서 서로 무슨 이야기를 그렇게 하고 있느냐?"

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse: "Que palavras [são] essas que vocês trocam entre si enquanto caminham?"
pt.B: Ele lhes perguntou: "Que conversa é essa que vocês estão tendo entre si pelo caminho?"
pt.R: Jesus perguntou a eles: "O que é isso que vocês estão conversando no caminho?"

am.L: እርሱም፦ «እየሄዳችሁ እርስ በርሳችሁ የምትለዋወጧቸው እነዚህ ቃሎች ምን [ናቸው]?» አላቸው።
am.B: እርሱም፦ «እየሄዳችሁ እርስ በርሳችሁ የምትነጋገሩት ምንድን ነው?» አላቸው።
am.R: ኢየሱስም፦ «በመንገድ ላይ እርስ በርሳችሁ የምትነጋገሩት ይህ ሁሉ ምንድን ነው?» ብሎ ጠየቃቸው።

decisions.choice: exchanging: tossing words back and forth
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw one thing against another. It pictures a lively exchange, each answering the other.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: Jesus to the two on the road: "các anh" (24:17-26); "các con" from 24:38
decisions.reason: While they do not know him, Jesus walks with them as a fellow traveller, and "các anh" is how a stranger speaks to grown men. Once he stands among the disciples as himself (24:38), he says "các con", as in John 20:19. A reviewer may prefer "các con" throughout.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the two in 해라체; they answer him in 합쇼체 with -시- and "저희" (24:18-24, 24:29), though they do not know him
decisions.reason: The speech levels settled for the Korean Gospels (style guide, section 4); a polite stranger is addressed in 합쇼체 by men who call themselves "저희".

source.text: καὶ ἐστάθησαν σκυθρωποί.

records.literal_gloss: And they stood still looking sad.

en.L: And they stood still, looking sad.
en.B: They stopped walking, and their faces were gloomy.
en.R: They stopped, and their faces looked very sad.

es.L: Y se detuvieron, con aspecto triste.
es.B: Ellos se detuvieron, con el rostro sombrío.
es.R: Se detuvieron, y sus caras se veían muy tristes.

fr.L: Et ils s’arrêtèrent, l’air triste.
fr.B: Ils s’arrêtèrent, le visage sombre.
fr.R: Ils se sont arrêtés. Ils avaient l’air très tristes.

sw.L: Nao wakasimama, wakiwa na nyuso za huzuni.
sw.B: Wakasimama, nyuso zao zikiwa na huzuni nzito.
sw.R: Wakasimama, na nyuso zao zilionekana zenye huzuni sana.

vi.L: Và họ đứng lại, mặt buồn rầu.
vi.B: Họ dừng lại, nét mặt buồn bã.
vi.R: Họ dừng lại, mặt mày rất buồn.

ko.L: 그러자 그들은 침울한 얼굴로 멈추어 섰다.
ko.B: 그들은 걸음을 멈추었다. 얼굴에는 슬픔이 가득했다.
ko.R: 그들은 걸음을 멈추었다. 그들의 얼굴은 몹시 슬퍼 보였다.

pt.L: E pararam, com o rosto triste.
pt.B: Eles pararam de andar, com o rosto abatido.
pt.R: Eles pararam, e o rosto deles mostrava muita tristeza.

am.L: እነርሱም አዝነው ቆሙ።
am.B: እነርሱም መሄዳቸውን አቁመው ቆሙ፤ ፊታቸውም በሐዘን ጠቁሮ ነበር።
am.R: እነርሱም ቆሙ፤ ፊታቸውም በጣም አዝኖ ነበር።
