fr.B: Ils se prosternèrent devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}adorer, puis regagnèrent Jérusalem avec une grande joie. \v 53 Et ils passaient tout leur temps dans la cour du temple, à bénir Dieu.
fr.R: Alors ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont adoré. Ils sont retournés à Jérusalem, remplis de joie. \v 53 Ils étaient toujours dans la cour du temple, où ils remerciaient et louaient Dieu.

sw.L: Nao, wakiisha kumwabudu, walirudi Yerusalemu kwa furaha kubwa, \v 53 nao walikuwa daima hekaluni wakimhimidi Mungu.
sw.B: Wakamsujudia na kumwabudu, kisha wakarudi Yerusalemu kwa furaha kubwa. \v 53 Wakawa wakikaa hekaluni muda wote, wakimhimidi Mungu.
sw.R: Kisha wakamwabudu. Wakarudi Yerusalemu wakiwa wamejaa furaha. \v 53 Walikuwa hekaluni kila wakati, wakimshukuru na kumsifu Mungu.

vi.L: Còn họ, sau khi thờ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem với niềm vui lớn, \v 53 và họ luôn luôn ở trong đền thờ, chúc tụng Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Họ sấp mình thờ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, rồi trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem, lòng tràn ngập niềm vui. \v 53 Họ luôn có mặt trong sân đền thờ, chúc tụng Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Rồi họ thờ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem, lòng đầy vui mừng. \v 53 Họ thường xuyên ở trong sân đền thờ, cảm tạ và ngợi khen Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그분께 경배하고 큰 기쁨으로 예루살렘으로 돌아가서, \v 53 늘 성전에서 하나님을 찬양하며 지냈다.
ko.B: 그들은 예수께 엎드려 경배하고, 크게 기뻐하며 예루살렘으로 돌아갔다. \v 53 그리고 늘 성전 뜰에서 하나님을 찬양하며 지냈다.
ko.R: 그들은 예수께 경배했다. 그리고 큰 기쁨에 차서 예루살렘으로 돌아갔다. \v 53 그들은 늘 성전 뜰에 모여 하나님께 감사하고 하나님을 찬양했다.

pt.L: E eles, depois de {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} adorarem, voltaram para Jerusalém com grande alegria \v 53 e estavam continuamente no templo, bendizendo a Deus.
pt.B: Eles se prostraram diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} em adoração e depois voltaram para Jerusalém com grande alegria. \v 53 E passavam todo o tempo no templo, bendizendo a Deus.
pt.R: Então eles {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} adoraram. Voltaram para Jerusalém cheios de alegria. \v 53 Estavam sempre no templo, dando graças e louvando a Deus.

am.L: እነርሱም ሰግደውለት በታላቅ ደስታ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ተመለሱ፤ \v 53 ዘወትርም እግዚአብሔርን እየባረኩ በቤተ መቅደስ ነበሩ።
am.B: እነርሱም በፊቱ ሰግደውለት በታላቅ ደስታ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ተመለሱ። \v 53 ጊዜያቸውንም ሁሉ እግዚአብሔርን እየባረኩ በቤተ መቅደስ ያሳልፉ ነበር።
am.R: ከዚያም ሰገዱለት። በደስታ ተሞልተው ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ተመለሱ። \v 53 ሁልጊዜም በቤተ መቅደስ ሆነው እግዚአብሔርን ያመሰግኑና ያከብሩ ነበር።

decisions.choice: having worshiped him: included, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the words left out, as in Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts
decisions.reason: Almost all manuscripts, the early papyrus P75 among them, have "having worshiped him". Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts lack it. Codex Bezae and some Old Latin manuscripts, known as Western witnesses, usually have a longer text than other manuscripts, but near the end of Luke they have a shorter text in several places. Where witnesses that tend to add leave something out, the shorter reading may be the original. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: worshiped him: bowed before Jesus as one bows before God
alternatives: honored him as a great man
decisions.reason: Jesus had told the devil that worship belongs to God alone (4:8). For the first time in Luke, his followers worship Jesus.

decisions.choice: with great joy: the joy the angel announced at his birth
decisions.reason: The angel brought the shepherds good news of great joy (2:10). The Gospel ends where it began, with joy and in the temple (1:8-9, 14).

decisions.choice: blessing God: praising and thanking God
decisions.reason: When people bless God they speak well of him, praising and thanking him, as Zechariah and Simeon did (1:64; 2:28).

decisions.choice: blessing God: the reading of the SBLGNT, with no "Amen"
alternatives: praising God, the reading of Codex Bezae
praising and blessing God, the reading of many manuscripts
Amen added at the end, as in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts, among them P75, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read "blessing". Codex Bezae reads "praising", and many later manuscripts join the two. Many later manuscripts also end the book with "Amen". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: in the temple: in the courts of the temple at the times of prayer
decisions.reason: The temple courts were open to worshipers, and the first believers met there daily (Acts 2:46; 3:1).

decisions.choice: giving thanks and praise to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what blessing God means.

decisions.choice: bowed down in worship before him
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out that the verb describes bowing low.

decisions.choice: habiéndolo adorado, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English "him" takes the setting, but in the Spanish participle the pronoun is joined to the verb, where there is nothing separate to capitalise. Balanced and Readable have a separate pronoun and take the span.

decisions.choice: l’ayant adoré (L); se prosternèrent devant lui pour l’adorer (B); l’ont adoré (R)
decisions.reason: The verb names bowing low before Jesus as one bows before God (m2). French "adorer" is the word for worship given to God, so every level uses it; Balanced also keeps the gesture, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: le temple (L); la cour du temple (B, R)
decisions.reason: This word names the whole temple area, and the disciples met in its courts at the times of prayer (m6); only priests entered the sanctuary. As the style guide has it, Literal says "le temple" and Balanced and Readable say where they were.

decisions.choice: wakimhimidi Mungu
decisions.reason: The term chosen for the Gospels when people bless God, that is praise and thank him (meaning decision m4); "kubariki" is kept for God or Jesus blessing people, as in verses 50 and 51.

decisions.choice: "thờ lạy"
decisions.reason: The word settled for proskyneō in the Vietnamese Matthew: bowing before Jesus as before God (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "đền thờ" (L); "sân đền thờ" (B, R) for hieron
decisions.reason: As the style guide gives for the whole temple area: they were in its courts (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "경배하다" for proskyneo; "찬양하다" for blessing God; "성전" (L), "성전 뜰" (B, R) for hieron
decisions.reason: "경배하다" as the Korean Luke 4:8 and Matthew 2; a person blesses God by praising him, as the Korean Luke 1:64; hieron is the temple area (docs/john-terms.md).

decisions.choice: "እግዚአብሔርን እየባረኩ" (blessing God)
decisions.reason: Amharic, like the Greek, can say that people bless God, meaning they praise him; Literal and Balanced keep the same verb as Jesus' blessing in 24:50-51, and Readable says thanks and praise, as the English Readable does.
